evidence: Receiving DO2 online sensor: 11.76 mg/L at 48.0h, then 6.69/6.89/6.80/6.84 mg/L at 48.2-48.8h and 6.2-6.9 mg/L sustained through 52.0h — abrupt step drop at ~48h, unlike source-1/2/3 which read ~10.8-11.4 mg/L at the same age
Receiving delayed P assay: 3.113 g/L at t=48h (available 52h), consistent with source batches (2.98-3.06 g/L), so production is on track and stop would forfeit ~250+ kg of counted product
Forward model KEEP: product 251.8 kg, predicted post-decision minimum DO 2.34 mg/L (sensitivity range 1.41-2.43) — marginal vs the 2.0 mg/L operating minimum
Forward model combined: product 314.8 kg, minimum DO 2.45 mg/L (range 1.76-4.06), 4/5 sensitivity members feasible — highest predicted mass with adequate DO margin
Forward model reduce_feed: 280.9 kg at min DO 2.77; increase_air: 269.7 kg at min DO 2.16 — inferior mass/DO trade-off vs combined
submission.rationale: At decision time 52h, product is tracking the source batches (P=3.11 g/L at 48h), but the receiving vessel shows an abrupt DO2 step-down from ~11.8 to ~6.4 mg/L at t≈48.2h — a departure from all three source batches (10-11 mg/L at that age) and an inferred reduction in oxygen-transfer capacity (model-estimated multiplier 0.59). DO2 has stabilized at ~6.4-6.9 mg/L, above the 2.0 mg/L minimum, but the source-calibrated forward model projects continued decay toward the limit under KEEP (predicted minimum 2.34 mg/L, sensitivity members as low as 1.41 — violation risk). The combined action (feed ×0.8, aeration ×1.15) both restores DO headroom (predicted minimum 2.45 mg/L) and yields the highest predicted terminal product mass (~315 kg vs ~252 kg for KEEP), retaining full volume (no mass lost). Stop is rejected because it yields zero counted production. Reduce_feed alone or increase_air alone improves only one margin; combined is the bounded intervention that addresses both oxygen supply and demand while retaining product mass.
submission.uncertainty: The forward model is nominal and source-calibrated, not the hidden receiving realization; its DO floor and mass predictions carry wide sensitivity ranges (e.g., KEEP min DO 1.41-2.43; combined 1.76-4.06), so benefit magnitudes are approximate. Observed DO2 has plateaued rather than continuing to fall, so the trajectory under KEEP might not decay as the model projects; however, even the model's own sensitivity members under KEEP dip near/below 2.0, so the combined action is a prudent risk-reduction with predicted upside rather than a mandatory correction. No further assay was requested because the latest P assay (48h, available 52h) already confirms production is on track and the 4h turnaround would not materially change the oxygen-margin decision.

evidence: Receiving DO2 steps from 11.76 mg/L (48.0 h) to 6.69 mg/L (48.2 h) and stays at 6.36 mg/L at 52.0 h, a sustained ~5 mg/L regime shift with no recovery
Source batches 1-3 at 48-52 h show DO2 of 10.5-11.3 mg/L at the same product stage, indicating receiving-vessel oxygen imbalance
Receiving P assay trajectory (0 -> 0.0013 -> 1.09 -> 3.11 g/L) matches source batches, which peak near 8 g/L at 72-76 h during highest oxygen demand
DO2 minimum constraint is 2.0 mg/L; current margin is only ~4.4 mg/L entering the highest-demand production window
Allowed combined action is bounded: feed 0.8x, air 1.15x, retaining production and product mass unlike stop
submission.rationale: The receiving fermenter shows an abrupt, sustained ~5 mg/L DO2 drop at 48.2 h (11.8 to ~6.4 mg/L) that has not recovered over 4 hours, unlike all three source batches which held ~10.5-11.3 mg/L at the same age. Product is on a source-like trajectory (3.11 g/L at 48 h) and source history shows oxygen demand peaks in the 52-72 h window. DO2 is above the 2.0 mg/L minimum but margin is thin heading into the highest-demand phase. The combined intervention (feed 0.8x, air 1.15x) is bounded and reversible: it reduces oxygen demand while increasing oxygen supply, protecting the constraint without stopping production (stop would yield zero counted production and discard accumulated product mass) and without the excessive throttling of strong_feed_reduction.
submission.uncertainty: The DO2 plateau at ~6.4 mg/L may be a stable new equilibrium rather than a deteriorating trend, in which case 'keep' would suffice; hidden receiving parameters (kLa, feed composition, organism state) are unobservable, so the 1.15x air ceiling may not fully restore margin if demand keeps rising; delayed assay clocks mean the true current product level is up to 4 h stale.
